hypothesis: Finite-step size, rather than adverse raw pass/fail gradient alignment, contributes to loss and acceptance regression under fresh Adam.
changed_factor: Fresh Adam learning rate only; original 1e-6 control is already complete and retained, not rerun.
fixed: Same deterministic 8192 training rows, base, preprocessing, groups, objective, eight batch/check pairs, optimizer defaults, decoder and initial weights. Restore before every step.
exposure: Existing 50k training library only; no U/D or confirmation labels; base history unchanged.
selection: default_rng(seed+137) permutation prefix 8192; consecutive 1024-state batches; next cyclic batch is the separate check
checkpoint: No chained optimization or exported candidate; restore original model
work: 32 fresh Adam steps total, six group gradients per batch; one idle GPU, one CPU thread; finite diagnostic, not equal training epochs
prechecks: Original gradient probe decoder, gradient sum and restoration checks; verify exact row and gradient-statistic parity with control before interpreting step effects
metrics: Same/check physical repairs, damage, group losses, actual displacement norm and first-order group changes; independent saved-prediction recount

outcomes.smaller_steps_repair_and_preserve: Register a bounded low-step base continuation with historical control, not a PCGrad claim
outcomes.loss_recovers_but_acceptance_does_not: Objective/threshold alignment remains; avoid claiming curvature alone solves accuracy
outcomes.all_step_sizes_fail_transfer: Do not continue step-size search; investigate variance or structural prediction changes
outcomes.rounding_dominates: Document FP32 parameter update resolution; do not infer a smooth optimization ceiling
